argument.text:
Fix tau>0 and real phases alpha,beta. Also, independently, fix a nonzero integer quadruple of zero sum. Assume L1 to collect these antecedent conditions. If either phase vanishes its covariance vanishes by its definition. For the remaining phase case use the following calculation.
 Let \(h(s)=e^{-i\alpha s}-M_\tau(e^{-i\alpha s})\). Then \(\eta_\tau=\tau^{-1}\int_0^\tau h(s)e^{-i\beta s}\,ds\). The elementary bound
\(|h(s)|\le\tau^{-1}\int_0^\tau|\alpha||s-r|\,dr\le\tau|\alpha|\)
gives the linear phase estimate, also interchanging \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Moreover,
\[
|h(0)|+|h(\tau)|\le\tau|\alpha|,\qquad
\int_0^\tau|h'(s)|\,ds=\tau|\alpha|.
\]
Integrating \(e^{-i\beta s}\) once gives \(|\eta_\tau|\le2|\alpha/\beta|\). Interchanging the phases proves the ratio estimate.

produces.statement: For these phases, eta=0 if alpha beta=0, and otherwise |eta|<=2 min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta|<=tau min(|alpha|,|beta|).

argument.text:
For the quadruple let A=|ab|, B0=|cd| and N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the sorted magnitudes. The largest magnitude is at most the sum of the other three, hence N1<=3N2.
 For the required ratio majorant, if \(d\) is among the two largest frequencies, use \(\min(A/B0,B0/A)\le1\). Otherwise the largest two are among \(a,b,c\). If they are \(a,b\), then
\[
\frac1{|d|}\min(A/B0,B0/A)\le\frac{|c|}{|ab|}\le\frac1{N_3}.
\]
If they are \(a,c\) (the case \(b,c\) is identical), their ratio is between \(1/3\) and \(3\). The remaining magnitudes are \(|b|,|d|\), whose maximum is \(N_3\). Thus
\[
\frac1{|d|}\min(A/B0,B0/A)\le3\min\left\{\frac{|b|}{|d|^2},\frac1{|b|}\right\}
\le\frac3{\max(|b|,|d|)}.
\]
For the required sum majorant, consider the pairing \((a,b)\) and \((c,d)\). If the two largest magnitudes are in the same pair, the other pair has sum of magnitude at most \(2N_3\). Since \(a+b=-(c+d)\),
\[
\frac{|a+b|}{\max(A,B0)}\le\frac{2N_3}{N_1N_2}\le\frac2{N_3}.
\]
If the largest two belong to different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them. Hence \(\max(A,B0)\ge N_2N_3\) and \(|a+b|\le2N_1\le6N_2\), giving the result. Ties can be ordered arbitrarily; the same alternatives cover them. 
This covers all placements and ties. Discharge L1 and universally quantify both independent choices to obtain the output.
